calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Devils are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Senators are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Senators.

calls.head: Bruisers against finesse
calls.body: The Senators hit a lot, but the Devils mostly don’t. Ottawa is near the top of the league for physicality, and New Jersey is one of the worst. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Senators.
calls.call: The Senators hit more than the Devils in the close stretches of the game.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Senators beat the Devils
paras: The Senators’ Nikolas Matinpalo left in the first period and didn’t return. Shane Pinto struck first for the Sens early in the second. Stephen Halliday stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play midway through the second. Tim Stützle made it 3-0 midway through the third. New Jersey had a goal taken off for goalie interference midway through the third. Arseny Gritsyuk got the Devils on the board 3:49 later. Tyler Kleven added an empty-net goal with 2:07 left to make it 4-1.
The chances were closer than the score. Linus Ullmark made 29 saves for the Senators, and Nico Daws stopped 16 of 19. The Senators improved to 5-1-0, and the Devils fell to 2-3-0.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Senators.
Shane Pinto scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 12.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
